I will play Monopoly as an AI player.

I am p1 with $529 cash and on VENTNOR_AVENUE after paying $22 rent to p4. I own the full orange set but have mortgaged NEW_YORK_AVENUE. I also hold ST_CHARLES_PLACE, STATES_AVENUE, ST_JAMES_PLACE, TENNESSEE_AVENUE, WATER_WORKS, and PARK_PLACE.

p2 has Boardwalk and two railroads but $286 cash. p3 owns the dark purple set with hotels and $785 cash. p4 has $1435.

p4 owns the light blue hotels and three yellows, leaving Atlantic Avenue unowned. I will not sell Park Place to p2 or p4, or St James and Tennessee. I will keep New York Avenue mortgaged until I can build three houses and survive a $600 rent hit.

Unmortgaging New York Avenue costs $110, leaving $419. I cannot build three houses yet because the orange set needs even housing across all three properties and requires roughly $1610 total. I will hold my cash and wait.

Unmortgaging New York Avenue would still leave only $119 after building one house on each orange property, which is too little to survive a hotel rent. Unmortgaging Park Place costs $193 and yields only $35 in rent, so it is not worth it either. I will avoid mortgaging unless I need cash for a debt. I am now considering trade offers that could help me gather enough cash to safely build three houses on the orange set.

p4 blocks my pink set with Virginia and will not sell cheaply. p3 owns the brown hotels and $785 cash. p4 is the biggest threat at $1435 with three light blue hotels. I am calculating exact orange rent values for three houses.

Mortgaging the pink properties and Water Works would raise only $215, bringing total cash to $744. That still falls $266 short of the $1010 needed for three houses on the orange set. I will hold this turn and look for a trade that raises cash without giving up the monopoly or Park Place.

Selling the pink properties to p4 would complete their pink monopoly and is too dangerous. Selling Water Works to p3 would give them both utilities, but that is less threatening than a color monopoly.

Water Works is worth only about $100 to $150, which is too little to bridge the cash gap. I cannot buy unowned properties from the bank. p2 has no useful pieces for me.

Boardwalk is not a viable trade target because p2 wants the dark blue monopoly and I already hold the other piece. Virginia costs $160 to buy normally, so p4 will not sell it cheaply; they need it to complete their own pink set and build another monopoly.

I will not sell my orange properties to p4, since they could use them to block my monopoly. p3 cannot complete the green set with only Pacific Avenue. I still have no way to acquire the unowned Illinois Avenue from the bank. I will hold this turn.

I am now considering a trade with p4 for Virginia. I could offer Park Place plus cash in exchange, since p4 does not own Boardwalk and might value the dark blue piece as a blocker against p2 or as an inheritance.

I will not sell Park Place to p4. That would give them dark blue potential and inheritance rights if I go bankrupt. Buying Virginia from p4 would cost too much cash. The pink set is also weaker than the orange set, so it offers no advantage.

Virginia is only useful as a second monopoly later, not now. I will end my turn.

I considered a public message to form an alliance against p4 with p2 and p3, but they may not trust me and I should not reveal my strategy.

I am roughly $266 short of even building three houses on the orange set, and $866 short of a safe buffer. p3 owns Baltic Avenue with a $450 hotel and Medford Avenue with a $250 hotel, so I would die to either of them if I build without cash. p2 has $286 and could survive a $600 Connecticut hotel hit with mortgaged railroads and Boardwalk, so he is not an immediate threat.

I will skip buying the unowned Illinois and Atlantic properties because they would leave me with too little cash for the orange set. I am now reconsidering selling Water Works to p3 for a high price, which would give them both utilities and raise my cash by roughly $150 to $200.

Selling Water Works to p3 would only net $75 in extra cash, so that trade is not worthwhile. I will end my turn. I also considered unmortgaging New York Avenue to start collecting double rent on the orange set, but realized that double rent does not apply while any property in the set remains mortgaged.

The timeline shows $28 rent on St James and Tennessee, but standard Monopoly rules say double rent is impossible while New York Avenue remains mortgaged. I am checking whether the game engine allows this exception.

The engine appears to be paying double rent on St James and Tennessee even though New York Avenue remains mortgaged. Unmortgaging it would cost $110 but only raise New York's rent from $0 to about $32, so the return is poor unless I am immediately building houses.

Unmortgaging New York Avenue would leave only $634, surviving one $600 hotel hit with just $34 remaining. The current cash plus mortgaged properties totals $744, which is enough to survive a single hotel but not two consecutive hits. Keeping the $110 unmortgage cost as survival cash is the safer choice.
